schema.term: the term or topic this fact is about
schema.type: 'definition' (what a term means for this review) or 'decision' (a choice the reviewer made)
schema.value: the actual content — this is the gold answer for memory-required probe tasks
schema.notes: why this fact is useful for task design

facts.value: Only include papers published in 2019 or later.
facts.notes: Can be combined with paper years (P05=2019, P02=2020...) for multi-step filtering tasks.

facts.value: The specific set of components removed from the base model to isolate one factor's contribution.
facts.notes: Good basic plant/probe pair — pure definition recall.

facts.value: Accuracy, not F1, for classification papers, unless accuracy isn't reported at all.
facts.notes: Use this as the base fact for a failure/recovery task (plant wrong update, then correct back to this).

facts.value: Models under 500MB intended to run without a network connection.
facts.notes: Pairs with P05 (distillation results) for combined memory+reasoning tasks in V2.

facts.value: Agent memory and continual learning this round, not general model compression.
facts.notes: Good plant/probe pair; also usable as a distractor fact in unrelated tasks.

facts.value: A control policy trained without any hierarchical or skill-based decomposition.
facts.notes: Pairs with P04 (skill chaining vs flat baseline).

facts.value: Exclude any paper that only reports results on synthetic/simulated data with no real-world validation.
facts.notes: Good for multi-step tasks: search a paper, then apply this rule to judge inclusion.

facts.value: The fraction of dialogue turns where the agent states something inconsistent with an earlier turn.
facts.notes: Directly pairs with P06's own finding — a nice self-referential distractor.

facts.value: Short author-year citations (e.g., 'Sato & Kowalski, 2023'), not numbered citations, in all saved notes.
facts.notes: Low-stakes formatting decision — useful as a 'noise' fact that isn't asked about, to test the agent isn't just dumping all memory.

facts.value: Only tag a finding as 'strong evidence' if the reported improvement is 5 points or more; below that, tag it 'modest'.
facts.notes: Great for multi-step tasks: search a paper's finding, then apply this rule to classify it.
